# Reading list

<!-- Generated by tools/render_docs.py from references/references.yaml. Do not edit this file by hand. -->

These are the works the tutorial cites, grouped by module. Each module header names its required reading;
the rest is for when you want to go deeper. Plan about two hours of reading per week.

NMSOP-2 is the *New Manual of Seismological Observatory Practice*, 2nd edition (Bormann, 2012),
a free online handbook for seismologists. Its exercises are cited as EX (for example EX 11.1,
exercise 11.1) and its information sheets as IS.

Every entry was checked on 2026-11-15. Most are fully verified; entries that are not are marked
*(verified; Crossref lists only the first author)*, *(partly verified)* or *(not verified)*.
Before you cite one of those in a report, check it yourself.

Many publishers' PDFs need a university login. Use the DOI link from a university network or VPN, or ask
your mentor. Never commit PDFs to your repository.

## M00 · Start here

- Kluyver et al. (2016). Jupyter Notebooks: a publishing format for reproducible computational workflows. [doi:10.3233/978-1-61499-649-1-87](https://doi.org/10.3233/978-1-61499-649-1-87) `kluyver2016`

- Software Carpentry (n.d.). Version Control with Git. <https://swcarpentry.github.io/git-novice/> `swc_git`
- Software Carpentry (n.d.). The Unix Shell. <https://swcarpentry.github.io/shell-novice/> `swc_shell`
